display: I coordinate a 22-woman Karen weaving cooperative in Mae Chaem, northern Thailand. We weave Karen patterns on backstrap and floor looms, using natural-dyed cotton and hemp.

signals.text: Twelve shawls in one blue are due in Chiang Mai by mid-October, and the dye has to stay steady for all of them.
We are short of undyed hemp. The supplier says two weeks, and we have orders waiting.
My natural-dye tests on hemp, with indigo and lac, gave two blotchy batches. The third looks promising, but I don't yet know why the first two failed.
Phone signal in the village is one bar, on a rock behind the temple. Calls with buyers break up and we end up settling colours by sending photos.
In the rainy season and again at rice harvest, most of us are in the fields. We rarely get more than six looms running, and from November the workshop will be nearly empty.
An NGO report is due at the end of October. My orders and design records are in a school notebook, and I type them up on borrowed phones.
I'm asked to give a speech about our weaving at the November temple fair. I'm a coordinator, not a speaker, and I'm nervous about it.
Some of the weavers are behind on orders because of harvest preparation, and I'm trying not to push them.
The headman wants us to host travel-agency guests on 20 October. I'm unsure how to do it without turning the workshop into a show.
The NGO funding that built our workshop ends next year, and I need other ways to keep the cooperative going.
In the village, nobody knows basic wound care, and the nearest clinic is ninety minutes away. Weavers' hand injuries get infected.
I'm afraid the young women will leave for factory work and the weaving will not pass on to them.
I finally finished a shawl myself, from my grandmother's zigzag pattern, and I want that work to reach people who will value it.

offers.text: A cooperative of 22 weavers working backstrap and floor looms, who can make Karen-pattern textiles to order.
Natural-dye cotton and hemp textiles, with indigo and lac dyes, and no chemical dyes.
A pattern archive of about 60 traditional Karen motifs, with the meaning and technique for each.
A shared workshop with six floor looms that could host a short residency, a research visit or a collaboration.
Buyers in Chiang Mai and Bangkok, and experience delivering small orders on a deadline.
I speak Karen, Thai and workable English, so I can be the link between outsiders and village weavers.
Local knowledge of a mountain village in Mae Chaem: seasons, farming, temple and community life.
Idle looms and weavers' time outside planting and harvest, which could fit custom work or a design collaboration.
Practical experience running a small cooperative: coordinating orders, keeping quality steady, and reporting to an NGO funder.

catchers.hypo: I'm a textile or dye researcher. I'd like to test how indigo and lac behave on hemp, and I could share what I find.
catchers.can: I can run test batches with the weavers and compare notes, since we already have two failed batches and one promising one.
catchers.confirm: Is your experience with natural dyes on hemp or similar bast fibres, not only on cotton or with synthetic dyes?

catchers.hypo: I'm a designer who wants to work with a traditional weaving group on a small line and pay a fair price for the work.
catchers.can: I can open the pattern archive to you, bring the weavers into the work, and plan production around harvest.
catchers.confirm: Are you willing to agree orders and timelines around the rice harvest, and to use only natural dyes?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nurse or medic, and I can run a one-day basic wound-care and hygiene session in a remote village.
catchers.can: I can arrange the workshop room, bring the weavers together, and translate between Karen and Thai.
catchers.confirm: Can you teach in Thai, or with a translator, in a village without a nearby clinic and with only basic supplies?

catchers.hypo: I'm a volunteer or student who has done NGO grant reporting and can help turn handwritten records into a clean report.
catchers.can: I can hand over the notebook figures, such as order counts and new designs, and you can help me format them. I won't share individual earnings.
catchers.confirm: Can you work from photos of a paper notebook, and are you fine with a report that leaves out individual weavers' earnings?

catchers.hypo: I'm an agriculture or soil scientist looking for a mountain village to host a field study this November.
catchers.can: My son studies agriculture in Chiang Mai and is looking for a soil project. I could introduce him and offer village access and local guidance.
catchers.confirm: Is your study about mountain soils or upland farming, and can it run in November?

catchers.hypo: I run a travel business and would like to bring small groups to see traditional weaving in a village.
catchers.can: Through the headman, I could discuss a limited visit. I'd set the number of guests, make sure the weavers agree, and keep it from becoming a performance.
catchers.confirm: Are you prepared to keep groups small, pay the weavers fairly, and fit the visit around the weavers' work schedule, without asking for staged shows?

catchers.hypo: I work on mobile connectivity or community networks and want to test a low-cost link in a place with almost no signal.
catchers.can: I can offer the village as a test site and give honest feedback on whether it works for taking orders and sending photos.
catchers.confirm: Does your solution work in a mountain village with one bar of signal and little power infrastructure?

catchers.hypo: I'm a young woman who left village life for factory work, and I miss craft. Is there a way to weave again, maybe remotely?
catchers.can: I can talk with you and, where it fits, offer a place at the looms or work on a design. Some of our weavers have faced the same choice.
catchers.confirm: Are you from a hill-tribe or rural family, and are you thinking about the same choice between factory work and weaving?

catchers.hypo: I'm a buyer or boutique owner who wants a small supply of natural-dye hemp or cotton textiles with a clear origin.
catchers.can: I can quote a realistic lead time, share colour samples by photo, and say honestly when the dye batch is not ready.
catchers.confirm: Can you accept natural-dye colour variation and a lead time of several weeks, not factory-exact matching?

catchers.hypo: I run a hemp or natural-fibre supply business and can sell undyed hemp in small, reliable lots to a cooperative.
catchers.can: I can place regular orders if the quality is right and delivery to Mae Chaem is possible.
catchers.confirm: Can you supply undyed hemp in small quantities, and deliver to a mountain district three hours from Chiang Mai?

forbids.text: No chemical dyes, ever. Our cloth is natural-dyed only.
I don't want the cooperative to become a tourist show or stage performances for visitors.
The looms cannot run during the November rice harvest, so no deadlines in that window.
I won't share any individual weaver's earnings or personal details.
I can't take on large factory-style volumes. The cooperative has 22 women and a limited number of looms.
I can't do long phone calls or video meetings. Signal is poor, so please use messages and photos.

projects.name: Natural dye experiments on hemp
projects.text: Testing indigo and lac on hemp. Two batches came out blotchy and the third looks promising. I'd like a partner to help find out why.

projects.name: Village temple fair stall
projects.text: A small weavers' stall at the 12 November temple fair, plus a plain-spoken talk about our weaving.

projects.name: Cooperative sustainability beyond NGO funding
projects.text: The NGO funding ends next year. I'd like to find fair buyers and new income routes without turning the weaving into a show.

policy.t1: When there is a real lead, I'll share our order cycle, the seasonal rhythm of looms and harvest, and our dye practice and tests.
policy.t2: Once trust is clear and I know who you are, I'll talk about health concerns in the village, family, and funding.
policy.never: Individual weavers' earnings, or anything that identifies a specific weaver's health, family or money.
